front: Jonas needs to paint pixel sprites, and Mira needs a vector logo that stays sharp on a poster. Which open source programs fit?
back: GIMP for photo and pixel (raster) editing; Inkscape for vector graphics, whose shapes scale without getting blurry.

front: Which open source programs are an office suite, an email client and a web browser?
back: LibreOffice (documents, spreadsheets, presentations), Thunderbird (email, calendar and news) and Firefox.

front: What is the difference between Chromium and Chrome?
back: Chromium is the open source browser. Chrome is Google’s browser built on it, with some proprietary parts added.

front: What is VSCodium?
back: A build of the open source code behind Visual Studio Code, without Microsoft’s added branding and tracking. It is a code editor.

front: What are VLC and GPG (GnuPG) for?
back: VLC plays almost any audio or video file. GPG encrypts and signs files and emails, and is a command line tool.

front: Which programs are a media center, a video-meeting tool, a classroom web-conferencing tool and a learning platform?
back: Kodi (media center), Jitsi (video meetings), BigBlueButton (virtual classrooms) and Moodle (courses, quizzes, grades).

front: Is Git a web application? How do GitLab, Forgejo and Gitea relate to it?
back: No. Git is the command line tool that tracks changes to source code. GitLab, Forgejo and Gitea are web services built around Git repositories.

front: Name two web servers and one common extra job of NGINX.
back: Apache HTTPD and NGINX. NGINX is also often used as a reverse proxy in front of other programs.

front: Which are the database servers in the exam list, and how are MariaDB and MySQL related?
back: MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL. MariaDB started as a fork of MySQL.

front: NFS or Samba: which shares files with Linux machines, and which with Windows?
back: NFS (Network File System) shares directories between Unix and Linux machines. Samba shares files and printers with Windows computers using their protocols.

front: What do Nextcloud and ownCloud give you?
back: Your own file sync and sharing "cloud", like Dropbox, with calendars and contacts, running on your own server.

front: What does LAMP stand for?
back: Linux, Apache, MariaDB or MySQL, and PHP: a well-known stack for running a website.

front: What is the difference between compiled and interpreted languages? Give examples.
back: Compiled languages (C, C++, Rust, Go) are translated into a machine-code program before running. Interpreted ones (Python, PHP, JavaScript, shell) are read by an interpreter. Java compiles to bytecode for a virtual machine.

front: Which language is Linux itself mostly written in, and which memory-safe systems language is used more and more near the kernel?
back: C is the language of Linux itself. Rust is the systems language with strong memory safety that is used more and more near the kernel.

front: Which languages are typical for browsers, for server-side web pages like WordPress and Moodle, and for network services created at Google?
back: JavaScript runs in browsers (and on servers through Node.js). PHP does server-side pages. Go is the fast, simple language from Google for network services and tools.

front: Which two extra languages did the 010-160 list include, and what are they?
back: Perl, an older scripting language popular for text processing and system tasks, and shell (usually Bash), the command language of the terminal.

front: What is the difference between a package and a repository?
back: A package is one file with a program, its data files and metadata (name, version, dependencies). A repository is a server holding many packages with an index the package manager downloads.

front: What is a dependency, and who resolves it for you?
back: A dependency is another package a program needs, such as a library. The package manager resolves it, so installing one program also installs what it needs.

front: Why can you trust software from your distribution’s repository?
back: The distribution runs the official repositories and signs each package, so your system can check where it came from.

front: Why do you normally install software from repositories instead of downloading installers?
back: One command installs, updates and removes software, resolves dependencies, and can update everything at once.

front: What is the difference between a low-level and a high-level package tool?
back: The low-level tool (`dpkg`, `rpm`) handles one package file and fetches nothing. The high-level tool (`apt`, `dnf`, `zypper`) talks to repositories, downloads what is needed and resolves dependencies.

front: Which package tools belong to Debian-based, Enterprise Linux, SUSE-based and Alpine systems?
back: Debian-based: `dpkg`, `apt`, `apt-get`. Enterprise Linux: `rpm`, `dnf`. SUSE: `rpm`, `zypper`. Alpine: `apk`.

front: What is the difference between `apt` and `apt-get`?
back: `apt` is the friendlier, newer front end for people at the keyboard. `apt-get` is the older one with a very stable interface, which scripts often use.

front: Mira downloads a `.deb` file and installs it with `dpkg`. Why might it fail where `apt` would work?
back: `dpkg` installs one package file and does not fetch dependencies. `apt` downloads the packages it needs from the repository.

front: Which commands refresh the package list, install `gimp` and remove it again on Debian?
back: `sudo apt update`, `sudo apt install gimp` and `sudo apt remove gimp`. They need administrator rights, hence `sudo`.

front: Which command lists installed packages on Debian, and which shows the package a file belongs to?
back: `dpkg -l` lists installed packages. `dpkg -S /bin/ls` shows the owner of a file: `coreutils: /bin/ls`.

front: Which package tool did the 010-160 exam list instead of `dnf`?
back: `yum`, the Red Hat family’s high-level tool before `dnf` replaced it. It does the same job (`yum install gimp`).

front: Which office suite did the 010-160 list name next to LibreOffice, and how are they related?
back: OpenOffice.org, the older suite from which LibreOffice was forked. It lives on as Apache OpenOffice.

front: What is a web application?
back: A program that runs on a server and that you use in your browser, so nothing is installed on your computer. Moodle, Jitsi and GitLab are examples.

front: Which components does LibreOffice have?
back: Writer (text), Calc (spreadsheets), Impress (slides), Draw (drawings), Math (formulas) and Base (databases). Native format: ODF.

front: What standard does GPG implement?
back: OpenPGP. A key pair lets you encrypt and sign: the public key is shared, the private key stays secret.

front: `apt remove` versus `apt purge`?
back: `remove` deletes the program but keeps its configuration files. `purge` deletes both. Both need root.

front: Static versus dynamic web content?
back: Static: a stored file sent unchanged. Dynamic: built by a program for each request, often from a database.
